text: Figures in brackets on the right hand side indicate full marks 1. Read the following case carefully and answer the questions below. Sania completed her MBA and got a job. She received her first salary and thought that she will buy a digital camera. She liked clicking pictures and loved sharing them with friends and reminiscence. A digital camera would make sharing pictures easy for her. She looked at a magazine. It gave the following details. Camera Specifications: Feature Nikon S 230 Kodak C160 Sony DSC W360 Megapixels 10 92 14.1 Optical Zoom 3X ; 3X 4x LCD screen size 3 inch 2.4 inches 3 inch Price Rs. 9,950 Rs. 7,999 Rs. 13,990 Other Image stabilizer, Smile   Face detection, blur   Double anti blur and blink detection detection sweep panaroma She took a dictionary and found out the meaning of the specific terms. She made following notes for herself. : e Pixel —Basic unit of image composition. Generally, the more your camera captures, the better. Manufacturers list their products' capabilities by the million, hence megapixels © Optical Zoom — Magnification of your field of view. Camera specs will list multiples of optical magnification based on a 35 mm camera (3x magnification equals 35-105 mm) e LCD Screen — Liquid Crystal Display; it's the multipurpose monitor on the back of the camera. Most folks prefer using this over the tiny, peek-a-boo viewfinder e Image stabilizer — Minimizes or prevents blurred images due to camera shake © Smile detection — Enables the camera to detect a smile and then click a photo automatically e Blink detection — Someone is always going to blink. It is the law of photography it seems. Blink detection automatically spots the blink and lets you know right away, giving you an opportunity of taking the picture again before everyone leaves the scene. e Face detection — camera detects faces in a scene and then automatically focuses (AF) and optimizes exposure (AE) and, if needed, flash output. e Blur detection — This is an indicator for giving a warning of ‘blur’resulted by the camera shake during clicking e Double anti blur — Lets you shoot in low light without flash to preserve the mood e Sweep Panaroma - The latest technology introduced for Digital camera to help user snapping pictures continuously on a horizontal position to get a super wide image. In the past, we’ll have to take a several times of pictures and join them up using image editing software like Photoshop. But the editing is eliminated with the Sweep panorama technology. Questions: (Each question carries 5 marks) 1) Explain the problem recognition stage in the consumer decision model in the context of Sania. 2) Where might she seek information about the digital cameras? text: Analyze the attached case study and give answers to the questions mentioned below it. PTO —— Yr Volvo reinvents itself through a strategy of market segmentation The importance of defining consumer segments is reflected in Volvo’s past strategy of identifying its cars with safety. The co. recognized that a segment of consumers emphasized car safety above all, & within reasonable limits, was willing to trade off style or comfort for safety. The typical demographic profile was a consumer who was married with two kids, made over $125,000 annually, & was in his/her mid to late 40’s. Throughout its history, the co. focused on safety as its sole defining feature, using tag line such as “a car you can believe in” & “drive safely”. By early 1990’s Volvo started to see sales dip. Volvo needed to increase car sales by increasing its appeal to a broader group of consumers; namely, empty nesters & young couples who were under 35, made more than $75000 annually, & had no children. This group comprised Gen X who valued performance & style above safety in car purchase decisions. To appeal to this group Volvo decided to re-position itself with a sportier, fun image without eroding its traditional safety message. It was a delicate balancing act. Its challenges were to appeal to Gen X & reconciling the consumer perception of its product in different countries. E.g. in USA Volvo was perceived as safe but upscale car; in UK mainly safe; in Far East upscale & prestige. The re-positioning effort began by changing the actual product line to appeal to the new target. It brought out C70 convertible. A $30million ad campaign was used to position the model with a tag line “yet another safe & practical family car from Volvo”. The co. partnered with AOL to develop a campaign using banner ads & promotion on internet to attract tech-oriented & 30+ customers. 500000 CD ROMs were distributed to current & potential owners to entrench itself in its new market. text: Elaboration Likelihood Model SECTION - B (Compulsory) 6. Read the case given below and answer the questions given at the end of the case. Attracting the Youth Segment Campbell Soup Company introduced its line of Chunky soups in Asia in late 90's. The product was geared to young people who were found to avoid the standard clear soup lines and were looking for something that tasted more like a meal. This heartier version of the soup containing more vegetables or meat in a heavier broth had done very well over the years with teens, particularly the young males in US market where it was the leading ready to serve food in super market. However, youth in Asia has been found to turn very often from soups to other foods for lunch and snacks, because of a high degree of prevalence of street food both traditional and contemporary. Cultural variable like food preferences and taste are also creating barriers for thc product. In addition with the faster penetration of microwave ovens and pizzas and popcorn cooked in them by college going youth as alternative snacks. In addition competitive ready-to-serve soups both from international and local market are gaining prominence, either on the plank of being an internationally known name or supplying local flavors to suit the Asian palate. Campbell has resolved to reach the youth and college market. It conducted specialized research on college canteens resulting in several interesting findings. First, only about 113 students use the college food facilities for lunch and only about one in four eat there for dinner. With 70% of the students having access to a heater or oven the potential exist for heating up soup. In addition this group likes soup and therefore is willing to consume chicken noodle soup or a variant of the corn soup rather than having heavy, full plate lunch. The trends of consumption are also changing. Six out of 10 college students in the metropolitan cities are more involved in buying prepared food than in the past. The students are usually short of time, especially during semesters. Thus, these patterns would indicate that heating up a   soup for a snack or a quick meal could be perceived as being fast and easy and would be an attractive food choice for these students College youths are an attractive market segment for several reasons. First they are a sizeable population in a lot of the Asian countries especially in South Asian countries. Second compared to others in their age group students typically have a discretionary income. Third because this is the time that many individuals are for the first time trying independent living and making consumption decision by themselves attracting them to Campbell brand could help to develop lifetime loyalty. Moreover, as university students, these consumers should become the leaders and innovators of tomorrow, enhancing the brands image in future. Campbell executives are also aware, however, that college students can be very difficult to reach and can be noticeable fickle in their brand choice behavior a) What in your view are the consumer behavior variables that the company should study before rolling out ts detailed marketing effort? b) Do you agree with the company's identification of the college going students as the most attractive segment? If the reference was specifically to the Indian market, which other segment would you suggest as being attractive for the company? c) Advise the company about appropriate promotional appeals to use for the product for the target segment of college student?
